verdict.rationale: Stripe Identity documents a programmatic Verification Sessions API that tracks each verification and returns results, plus webhook events on every status change. Its machine-readable OpenAPI spec includes the identity.verification_session schemas, so an agent can read outcomes and branch on status. However, the pack never shows granular per-check results, risk scores or signals, or structured failure-reason codes. Missing for 10: documented per-check result fields, risk signals/scores, structured failure-reason codes, independent or hands-on corroboration of agent branching on outcomes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, verification outcomes come back structured enough for an agent to decide on — machine-readable check results, risk signals, and failure reasons an automated onboarding flow can branch on

citations.quote: This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
You can access most verification details programmatically... using your secret key.
Listen for verification results so your integration can automatically trigger reactions.
Stripe generates events every time a session changes status.
The published spec3.json itself carries the Identity resources (identity.verification_session and related schemas), so the Identity API is machine-readable through the platform spec.
